title: We built a crafting system that generates entirely new items using AI during gameplay
author: ChromaGolem
selftext:
We're developing Alchemy Survivors, a roguelite where players can combine existing items or type a wish to create something entirely new during a run.

When the game encounters a new combination or wish, it sends a request to our own AI content service, which generates the item's stats, description and sprite. The resulting item is then saved and becomes usable equipment.

One of the more interesting design challenges with this system is balancing player creativity against the game's progression and combat mechanics.

Curious how other developers approach balancing procedurally generated equipment.

comments.author: ChromaGolem

comments.author: VortexAssetStudio
comments.body:
The visual consistency side of runtime sprite generation is just as tricky as the stat balancing. Usually, if you don't lock down strict lighting and framing rules in the prompt pipeline, the newly generated gear ends up clashing hard with the base inventory icons.

For the stats, tying the player's "wish" to a hidden rarity budget (where stronger keywords automatically add negative trade-offs or higher mana/cooldown costs) keeps things from breaking early runs while still letting players feel clever. Cool concept!
